title: Completed integral coefficient projections and regular scalar powers
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $O$ and uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and any scheme $T$. On its small pro-etale site put $R=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ with its actual projections to the constant quotient ring sheaves $C_j=(O/\pi^j)_T$ and $B_n=(O/\ell^n)_T$ for $j,n\geq1$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. There exist $u\in O^\times$ and $e\geq1$ such that $\ell=u\pi^e$; the ideals $(\ell^n)$ and $(\pi^j)$ are cofinal, and all rings $O/\pi^j$ and $O/\ell^n$ are finite. On sections over every site object, multiplication by each positive power of $\pi$ or $\ell$ is injective on $R$. The actual projection $\rho_j:R\to C_j$ is an epimorphism of sheaves of rings and its kernel is the ideal sheaf $\pi^jR$. Likewise $q_n:R\to B_n$ is an epimorphism with kernel $\ell^nR$. Thus the canonical maps induce ring-sheaf isomorphisms $R/\pi^jR\xrightarrow{\sim}C_j$ and $R/\ell^nR\xrightarrow{\sim}B_n$, normalized by the projections and compatible with every quotient transition. Quotients here are sheaf quotients (sheafification of sectionwise quotients), and $\pi,\ell$ act by their constant scalar sections; no characteristic or finiteness condition on $T$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply DVR factorization to the nonzero scalar ell. Its absolute value is strictly less than one, so it is not a unit and the uniformizer exponent e is positive. Equality (ell)=(pi)^e and the existing cofinality theorem give cofinal positive filtrations. Use Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing for the uniformizer quotients; rewriting (ell)^(n+1)=(pi)^(e(n+1)) gives finiteness of the ell quotients.

proof.text: A surjective homomorphism of coefficient rings has a set-theoretic section. Apply constant set sheafification to this section and transport through constantCommuteCompose for the underlying-set functor. This proves surjectivity on sections of the constant ring quotient map. Factor it through the normalized completed projection; that projection is therefore surjective on every site object, and cancellation on sections proves it is epi.

proof.text: For the uniformizer projection, completedIntegralProjection_divisible writes every kernel element as pi^(n+1)y. Conversely scalar normalization and quotient ideal membership show that every such product maps to zero. Thus the kernel is exactly the sectionPowerIdeal. Apply completedIntegralScalar_regular for injectivity of every uniformizer power.

proof.text: To calculate the ell projection kernel, identify its ideal with the uniformizer ideal of exponent e(n+1). Equality elimination reduces its target to that uniformizer quotient, and completedIntegralFiniteQuotientHom_ext identifies the two normalized projections. Transfer the kernel formula. The scalar ring homomorphism sends ell=u*pi^e to the same identity in completed sections. Its unit factor gives equality of principal ideals and permits cancellation, proving regularity of ell powers.

proof.text: For either scalar power, form the natural transformation from sectionwise quotient rings to the constant finite quotient, using the proved kernel formula. Each component is bijective by the first isomorphism theorem and sectionwise surjectivity, so it is an isomorphism of presheaves. Sheafify this isomorphism and compose with the counit at the target sheaf. Naturality of the sheafification unit and the adjunction triangle identity prove that the resulting isomorphism is normalized by the actual projection.
